organizations.normalization_notes: The wartime department is preserved under its historical name and is not silently replaced by a modern successor.

The historically named Intelligence Corps is kept distinct from the British Army as a whole. Its parent-service relationship remains descriptive until the organization model supports parent links in reviewed imports.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: security part of the War Office
affiliations.date_precision: approximate years; the transcript says the War Office period preceded Army entry in 1942 or 1943
affiliations.research_notes: Ramsbotham directly recalled security work at the War Office before entering the Army. The accessible transcript does not establish the sequence relative to his OSS-indexed connection, so this is neither an immediate-pre-OSS nor a civilian-employer claim.

affiliations.role_title: Captain, later major and GSOII at army headquarters
affiliations.date_precision: approximate wartime years reconstructed from the oral-history sequence; exact dates are not stated on the reviewed pages
affiliations.research_notes: The first-person transcript documents Intelligence Corps service and a rise from captain to major, matching the index's uncommon name and major rank. It does not establish whether this assignment preceded, overlapped, or followed the indexed OSS relationship.

claims.claim_text: The index contains two separately printed Tommie I records with variant surnames and different boxes but the same protected identifier; their relationship remains conflicting pending archival review.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Rammage Tommie I ... Remmage Tommie I
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Visual review confirmed Rammage on page 383 and Remmage on page 388. The shared private identifier creates a strong duplication signal but does not justify silently merging the rows.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting: the identifier suggests one person, while the printed surname spelling and box placement differ. Both source records remain separate.
claims.temporal_assessment: The index establishes wartime personnel-file entries but supplies no pre-OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: The public profile discloses the duplicate conflict without displaying the protected identifier. Boxes 632 and 639 require comparison.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Peter E Ramsbotham is a high-confidence match to Sir Peter Edward Ramsbotham, who recalled wartime British intelligence service and promotion to major.
claims.evidence_excerpt: captain, then major GSOII at army HQ
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The first-person oral history expands the uncommon indexed name and describes wartime intelligence duties at a rank compatible with the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name, middle-name expansion, compatible major rank, and documented wartime intelligence context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The transcript documents wartime assignments but does not establish when or how Ramsbotham entered the OSS index.
claims.match_notes: The institutional first-person source resolves identity strongly; it does not authorize an immediate-pre-OSS or civilian-employer inference.

claims.claim_text: Peter Ramsbotham recalled security work in the British War Office before Army service; its relationship to his OSS-indexed connection is uncertain.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I went for some time to the security part of the War Office
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Ramsbotham said he moved into War Office security work after war began and before he entered the Army in 1942 or 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the uncommon name, expanded middle name, major rank, and wartime intelligence context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly before Army service, but the accessible source does not establish its sequence relative to the indexed OSS relationship.
claims.match_notes: Published as a qualified government assignment only. It is not labeled a civilian employer or immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Peter Ramsbotham recalled wartime service in the British Army Intelligence Corps, including work as a captain and later major; its OSS sequence is uncertain.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I went back then into the Intelligence Corps
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His oral history describes Intelligence Corps service, special counter-intelligence work after D-Day, and work as captain then major at army headquarters.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the uncommon name, expanded middle name, compatible major rank, and wartime intelligence context.
claims.temporal_assessment: The assignment is documented during the war, but the accessible source does not establish whether it preceded, overlapped, or followed the indexed OSS relationship.
claims.match_notes: Published as a qualified military assignment only, with temporal uncertainty visible and no immediate-pre-OSS inference.
